issues: Dashboard tab set diverges from spec: request asks for 'Stock Intake, POS Billing, Sales History, Replenishment, Telemetry, Security & Recalls' (6 tabs). Actual UI renders 5 tabs: 'Batch Intake, POS Billing, Replenishment, Sales History, Analytics'.
'Telemetry' tab is labelled 'Analytics' (renamed) — backend endpoints /pharmacy/telemetry/{volumetric,spatial,timeline} still exist and return data.

No dedicated 'Security & Recalls' tab even though /pharmacy/security-alerts and /pharmacy/recalls return seeded records (15+ alerts, 5+ recalls). These are currently only surfaced inside Analytics/other views; user-visible tab missing.

action_items: Consider adding a dedicated 'Security & Recalls' tab (or renaming Analytics → 'Telemetry & Alerts') so the seeded /pharmacy/security-alerts + /pharmacy/recalls data has a first-class UI surface (matches spec).
Optional: align tab label with request — 'Batch Intake' → 'Stock Intake', 'Analytics' → 'Telemetry' — if the PRD language is meant to be canonical.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1167 lines — split into APIRouter modules (auth, pharmacy_ops, telemetry, consumer) per <code_review_guidelines> (>700-line rule).
GET /api/consumer/openfda uses query param name `q`, but the review request/PRD refers to `?drug=`. Either accept both aliases or update the docs to say `q`.

ConsumerVerifyPayload has no `medicine_name` field — the spec example ships `medicine_name` in the request body. It is silently ignored today (extra fields tolerated by Pydantic default). Either add the field and use it as a tie-breaker when the same batch normalises across products, or explicitly reject unknown keys.

risk_bucket mid-band returns severity string 'Quality Risk' for 80-94 — the review request wording expects 'Critical' at >=80. Batches with scores in 80-94 will therefore surface as 'Quality Risk', not 'Critical'. Confirm the 3-tier taxonomy is intentional (Critical / Quality Risk / Clear) vs the 2-tier one in the spec (Critical / Advisory / Clear).
TestStockIntake fixture uses class-scoped instance-method fixture — pytest emits PytestRemovedIn10Warning; convert to @classmethod.
